account: Today I read my appointments and held morning office hours. The secretary reported no new correspondence and no firsthand mill concerns from Baker or Neighbour, but had been unable to find the miller yesterday evening or early today. I arrived at the mill just before ten for my scheduled grain inspection; I have not yet seen the miller or inspected the grain. Several townsfolk nearby are repeating an unusual, unclear report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk 21 said Baker was there, that Baker and Neighbour were there, and that the innkeeper carried a sack of bread at the bakery. Neighbour has now arrived nearby. I do not know what actually changed or why; the repeated report is not enough to establish a transport problem or any wrongdoing. The bread sack could simply reflect a large bread purchase. I should seek a firsthand explanation from Neighbour or Baker. Builder also visited the office and requested a brief great hall lighting inspection at eighteen today, offering to fetch me beforehand. I agreed and asked the secretary to record it. This appears to be hall maintenance, though I have not yet seen any lighting fault. My remaining scheduled business includes lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, cottage tea with Neighbour at three, afternoon office hours, the lighting inspection, and home at seven.
